tasks.title: Chop-rebuild frame hitch follow-up (BUILD 1061)
tasks.verification: DONE (BUILD 1080, commit 66fa66bf, parent-verified 2026-11-16): profile finding (measured, not guessed): the generator 266 chunks are already fine-grained (slowest chunk 11.4ms) — the bottleneck was the renderer driver budget rule, not any single chunk. The driver passed Infinity while the player was stationary, so a chop ran the whole ~200-400ms rebuild in ONE frame (the 367-417ms hitch from BUILD 1061). Fix: a new rebuildUrgent ref (view -> BuildingContext -> WorldRendererDeps). Only an URGENT rebuild (enter/exit a hut, where the shell-hide interior must appear in the same frame) runs to completion; every other rebuild gets the 10ms step budget, moving or not. The buffer is bit-identical either way. The stale BUILD 1035 comment documenting the old budget rule was updated with it. Parent verification: origin/main 66fa66bf (on top of studio fa4d0369); tree clean; served version.json 1080 + __AG_BUILD 1080; standalone asserts 20 passed (parent re-ran directly, all 20 ok lines printed — ALL 1080 ASSERTS PASSED — the 10ms slice keeps every step <50ms (max 41.3ms); the Infinity path costs 225.4ms in one call — the old hitch, measured; enter/exit flag urgent; the sliced result is bit-identical to the sync build); tsc exit 0; sim 385,439/51 vs pristine 385,439/51 (IDENTICAL totals — no M1080 sim section, the worker covered the fix with 20 standalone asserts instead; zero new failures, fail lists byte-identical — parent re-ran the modified sim directly: 385,439/51, matching the worker); M1069 24h numbers IDENTICAL to the 1079 baseline (wood 48/48/24, grain 16/16, meals 8/27, deliver jobs 32, final wood 24, food 11, population 6) — a performance fix changed nothing in the sim, as required; probe 0 page errors, boot renders correctly (sha256 matches the 1078 boot screenshot — same scene, clock 8:03 AM), playing Day 1 8:22 AM (Placed Grass, wood 2, camp wood 2, the Build panel with Remove/Undo/Redo buttons visible), E-key chop gains wood (0 -> 2), UI placement lands (count 4 -> 5), hut door Enter/Exit works (inside hut rect 126..129 x 119..121, Enter rebuild 1 frame), Control Center all 10 sections, reload exact (placements 7 -> 7, player wood 2 -> 2, HUD renders). Frame time, before vs after (same Playwright harness, 390x844, SwiftShader, pristine 1079 on 8902 vs fixed 1080 on 8901): chop rebuild 1 frame / maxStep 419.9ms / rAF max gap 300.0ms (before) -> 20 frames / maxStep 60.6ms / rAF max gap 200.0ms (after) — the rebuild is now time-sliced over 20 frames, the worst single step dropped 7x; load build (bonus) 1 frame / 419.9ms -> 28 frames / 41.2ms — the boot hitch is gone too; Enter (urgent path) 2 frames on pristine -> 1 frame / 225.9ms on fixed — the urgent flag works, and it also fixed Enter (on pristine the player moves 1 tile on enter, so it got the 10ms budget and took 2 frames). Honest note on the rAF numbers: SwiftShader draw costs ~183ms/frame, so the rAF gaps are dominated by the draw, not the rebuild. On a real phone the draw is ~8ms/frame (per the 1035 comment), so the phone chop frame goes from ~200-400ms (rebuild-dominated) to ~18-28ms (draw + one 10ms step). The mechanism is proven by the step counts (1 -> 20 frames, maxStep 419.9 -> 60.6ms); the phone improvement follows from the draw cost, not from a phone measurement. The pristine probe failed at the Enter check as expected (Enter took 2 frames there) — which is itself the proof the probe distinguishes before from after. BENCHMARK: duration 938s (16 min, spawn 08:49:34Z -> live 09:05:12Z) vs 25-min baseline — UNDER, the TENTH build under it (a genuine improvement: faster AND regression-free AND full functionality); top file Engine3DWorldView.tsx 2 edit calls (1 scripted application + 1 comment-only edit), under the 3-edit warning and the 4-edit hard stop; files 5; regressions 0. tasks.brief: Fix the delivery strand found by the J-1 diagnostic (verify1065/diag1065.mjs): after the hut is done, a founder who flips to rest/eat while carrying wood strands the delivery — Greta and Perrin carried 2 wood each for 115+ seconds without delivering (completed stuck at 17, pile stuck at 14). Root cause: the delivery branch and founderDestination are gated on activity being work/build — a resting/eating carrier walks to the rest/eat tile, not the stockpile, and the delivery never fires. Fix: make delivery execute by workState, not activity (a carrying founder heads to the camp centre and delivers regardless of activity). It is self-limiting and does not block the hut chain or 0x06. Verify with a diagnostic that a carrying founder who flips to rest/eat still delivers within a bounded time.

tasks.title: Food-loop fix — make food drive work so a finished settlement farms
tasks.brief: The 24-hour test (0x09) proved a finished settlement starves: once both huts are done and the wood pile is full, the work score drops to ~0.05 and loses to rest/sleep/eat, so no founder activity is work, so nobody claims a harvest job, so the farm never runs and food drains 30 to 0. Fix: add a food term to the utility scorer (or a food-aware work assignment) so a founder works when the camp is short of food. The fix touches the core decision layer (utility.ts) and the pinned M1059 scorer asserts — update those asserts to the new behavior, do not weaken them. The 24h test (M1069) must go green after this fix. Keep the settlementSim driver in sync (it mirrors the scorer).
